**Rapid‑Mode Redesign – 30‑minute Introductory Lesson  
“Observation vs. Inference”**

---

## 1.  Lesson Purpose & Alignment  

| Element | Draft Specification |
|---|---|
| **Course context** | First week of an introductory science or general‑education course (e.g., Intro to Biology, Chemistry, or Critical Thinking). |
| **Target audience** | Undergraduate students, mixed abilities, first‑year. |
| **Delivery mode** | Short‑lecture + active‑learning micro‑practice; assumes a classroom with projector or a synchronous‑online video‑conference that supports screen‑share, breakout rooms, and a poll/quiz tool (e.g., Zoom + Mentimeter or LMS quiz). |
| **Time budget** | 30 min total (5 min intro, 10 min guided practice, 10 min collaborative task, 5 min debrief/exit ticket). |
| **Learning outcome (Bloom‑based)** | **C1 – Understand**: *Students will be able to differentiate an observation from an inference, and correctly label each statement in a short scientific description.* |
| **Evidence of learning** | Formative exit‑ticket items (two short statements to classify) + in‑class quick‑poll accuracy data. |
| **Cognitive demand token** | `understand` (single‑step classification). |
| **Pedagogical format** | “Think‑Pair‑Share” + “Immediate feedback poll”. |
| **Accessibility** | All visual slides will have alt‑text; captions for recorded audio; colour contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA; activity instructions provided as plain‑text handout and screen‑reader‑friendly PDF. |
| **Safety** | No lab or physical hazard – safety review **blocked** (no hazard). |

---

## 2.  Detailed Lesson Storyboard (30 min)

| Time | Segment | Content & Instructor Moves | Student Activity | Media / Materials |
|------|---------|----------------------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **0‑5 min** | **Hook & Definitions** | 1. Show a 30‑sec video clip of a scientist in the field (e.g., a rainforest canopy). 2. Prompt: “What do you *see* in the clip? What do you *think* is happening?” 3. Define **Observation** (direct sensory data) and **Inference** (interpretation/ explanation). | Jot down one observation and one inference on a digital sticky‑note or paper. | Slide 1 (video embed), Slide 2 (definition table), sticky‑note/Google‑Jamboard. |
| **5‑15 min** | **Guided Practice (Poll + Immediate Feedback)** | 1. Present three short sentence cards (mixed). 2. Launch an LMS poll: label each as O or I. 3. Reveal answers, discuss why each is an observation or inference, highlighting cue words (“looks”, “appears” vs. “suggests”, “likely”). | Individually answer poll; then view class‑wide histogram. | Slides 3‑5 (sentence cards), poll tool (Mentimeter/LMS). |
| **15‑25 min** | **Collaborative Task (Think‑Pair‑Share)** | 1. Hand out a 150‑word paragraph describing a simple experiment (e.g., “When the beaker is heated, the solution turns cloudy…”). 2. In pairs, label each statement as O or I. 3. Pairs submit a shared Google‑Doc with colour‑coded labels (green = O, orange = I). 4. Instructor samples two pairs, discusses. | Pair work → edit shared doc → brief whole‑class share. | Handout PDF, shared Google‑Doc, slide 6 (task instructions). |
| **25‑30 min** | **Exit Ticket & Wrap‑up** | 1. Two new sentences appear on slide; students submit via LMS “short‑answer” whether O or I. 2. Quick summary: why the distinction matters for scientific reasoning. | Submit responses; view aggregate correctness. | Slide 7 (exit tickets), LMS quiz. |

---

## 3.  Instructional Supports  

| Support | Rationale (Evidence‑Informed) |
|---|---|
| **Visual cue‑word list** (e.g., “is/are”, “looks like” → Observation; “suggests”, “means” → Inference) | Reduces cognitive load by making lexical markers explicit (Chi, 2006). |
| **Immediate feedback poll** | Provides formative data; short‑latency feedback improves knowledge retention (Bangert‑Drowns et al., 2015). |
| **Colour‑coded collaborative document** | Supports multimodal representation (dual‑coding) and peer articulation of reasoning. |
| **Exit‑ticket** | Summative check of the single‑step classification; data feeds into next‑day lesson planning. |
| **Universal Design for Learning (UDL) layering** | Multiple means of representation (video, text, audio), expression (poll, sticky‑note, doc), and engagement (pair work). |

---

## 4.  Assessment Blueprint (Formative)

| Item | Prompt | Desired response | Scoring rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Poll Q1‑3** | “Label Sentence 1 as Observation or Inference.” (3 items) | Single‑choice correct label. | 1 pt each; total 3 pts. |
| **Collaborative Doc** | Colour‑code each statement (O/I). | All correct colour assignments. | Binary pass/fail for rubric (teacher reviews a random 20 % sample). |
| **Exit‑Ticket (2 items)** | “Sentence A – Observation or Inference?” (2 items) | Correct label. | 1 pt each; total 2 pts. |

*Total possible points = 5 + 2 = 7. The exit‑ticket can be used as a quick mastery check (>80 % correct = mastery).*

**Rubric sketch (teacher‑facing)**  

| Criterion | 3 – Exceeds | 2 – Meets | 1 – Below |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Correct classification** | All statements correctly labelled (100 %). | 1‑2 errors (≈70‑90 %). | >2 errors (<70 %). |
| **Explanation of why** *(optional, for richer feedback)* | Provides clear rationale linking cue‑words. | Minimal rationale (single cue word). | No rationale or incorrect rationale. |

*Rubric is **objective‑achievement** oriented (single correct answer).*

---
